paper.title: Beyond Numeric Rewards: In-Context Dueling Bandits with LLM Agents

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed dueling bandits with Condorcet winner (TO, SST, STI), LLM-recommended arms
unmapped: Preference matrix satisfies Total Ordering, Strong Stochastic Transitivity and Stochastic Triangle Inequality (Assumptions 1-3)
Learner receives arm-pair recommendations from an LLM agent (possibly adversarial) as side advice
The learner knows the threshold eps_12 (epsilon_{1,2}) used in Match Arms
Paper writes the Condorcet-winner condition as epsilon_ij > 1/2 although epsilon_ij is in (-1/2,1/2) (notational inconsistency)
settings.definition_quote: a learner interacts with the environment by selecting two arms Arm_1(t) and Arm_2(t) from a set of K arms {b_1,...,b_K} for a noisy comparison (a duel)... the event that an arm b_i wins against b_j is a Bernoulli random variable with a parameter denoted by Pr(b_i > b_j).

settings.name_in_paper: Dueling bandits with a prompt-manipulating attacker (standalone LLM agents) (lower bound)
unmapped: An attacker with budget Phi(T) manipulates the LLM's input prompt to remove the optimal arm from the duel with probability p
settings.definition_quote: We consider an attacker with a budget Phi(T) who employs the following strategy: whenever the LLM agent selects the optimal arm b^* for comparison, the attacker manipulates the input prompt to the LLM to eliminate b^* from the duel with probability p

symbols.eps_12: distinguishability epsilon_{1,2} between the best and second-best arm (used as threshold)

tuning: delta = 1/(T K^2) in IF2/Validate, delta = 1/(K^2 log T) in Match Arms

results.notes: Strong regret defined via preference gaps (pseudo-regret). Text says this holds regardless of LLM behaviour; Õ hides polylog(T).

conditions: any standalone LLM agent whose policy is represented by Eq.(1) and whose worst-case behavior under the original prompt is uniform random pair selection (Assumption 4)
there exists a preference structure and attacker strategy

source.label: thm:vulnerable_llm
source.quote: For the dueling bandits problem with $K$ arms and time horizon $T$, there exists a preference structure and an attacker strategy with budget $\Phi(T)$, such that any standalone LLM agent, whose policy is represented by Eq.(\ref{eq:policy}) and whose worst-case behavior under the original prompt satisfying Assumption~\ref{assump:1}, will suffer an expected regret of $\Omega\left(\min\left\{\Phi(T), {T}/{K}\right\}\right)$.

results.notes: Hidden constants p (attack probability) and epsilon (gap). Regret type unspecified ('expected regret'); mapped to pseudo-regret.

symbols.T_LLM: time after which LLM recommendations contain the best arm

conditions: algorithms ALG satisfying E[WR(ALG)] <= T_LLM (for all T_LLM)
LLM agent recommending arms chosen adversarially

source.label: thm:converse
source.quote: Given any algorithm $\textsc{ALG}$ for dueling bandits, there exists an LLM agent recommending arms such that if $\textsc{ALG}$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{WR}(\textsc{ALG})]\leq T_{\mathrm{LLM}}$ ..., then it must hold that ${\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{SR}(\textsc{ALG})]\geq \mathbb{E}[\mathsf{WR}(\textsc{ALG})] = \Omega(T)}$.

results.notes: Applies to both weak and strong regret; informal converse statement.
